newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: PRESS DIGEST - New Zealand newspapers - July 17.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - New Zealand newspapers - July 17.

text.p: THE DOMINION

Kopu abandons Alliance: Dissident MP Alamein Kopu abandoned the Alliance on Wednesday night, pledging to be an independent MP representing Maori people, and said she would speak in parliament only in Maori. Page 1.
Head of Treasury resigns: Treasury head Murray Horn raised eyebrows on Wednesday when he resigned as head of the government's premier policy agency. Page 1.

CYPFS in the clear over MP's allegations: Retired Youth Court judge Mick Brown has found no evidence to support allegations that welfare staff falsified documentation surrounding children's deaths. Page 2.

'No' to super may be 'no' to future tax cuts: Treasurer Winston Peters indicated on Wednesday that a no vote in September's referendum on his controversial superannuation scheme could put an end to further tax cuts. Page 2.

Kiwi nose-dives against US dollar: The New Zealand dollar would continue to fall to about US63 cents during the next three months and could be as low as US60 cents by Christmas, a foreign exchange dealer said on Wednesday. Page 15.
Network job losses predicted: The Radio Network is pinning its future on a $10 million technology investment that "niches" its New Zealand stations and cuts 200 jobs in the process. Page 15.

Manufacturers' June quarter worst on record, says NZIER: Manufacturers had their worst quarter on record in the three months to June, according to the New Zealand Institute of Economic Research's survey of business opinion. Page 15.

Tax expert urges 'conduit' extension: The government should extend the "conduit" proposal for the taxation of foreigners' dividends and drop the 15 percent withholding tax, KPMG national tax chairman Chris Abbiss said on Wednesday. Page 16.
THE NEW ZEALAND HERALD

NZ First toasts Kopu: Alamein Kopu's first appointment after resigning from the Alliance last night was to attend a celebration hosted for her by the New Zealand First deputy leader, Tau Henare, in Parliament's Grand Hall.
Litigation fears over cuts at Patent Office: A restructuring of the Patent Office resulting in wholesale job cuts has raised concerns that it could lead to a more litigious environment.
Clear sues Telecom, govt for damages: The government and Telecom are being sued for damages by Clear Communications in an action filed on Wednesday in the High Court.
NZ may get digital radio soon: New Zealanders could be tuning into digital radio within the next three years, former Radio New Zealand head Nigel Milan predicted on Wednesday.
Donaghy's plans to stop making products in NZ: Manufacturing group Donaghy's plans to progressively stop making products in New Zealand.

Ansett starts freight service: Ansett International Air Frieght, a subsidiary of Ansett Australia, has begun its own air freight service between Auckland and Sydney to replace a joint venture arrangement with DHL.
Closures of plants seen as inevitable: Meat plant closures in the North Island are inevitable, says the Minister of Agriculture, Lockwood Smith.
THE PRESS

Tax-based pensions will lead to poverty, says MP: New Zealand's economy would collapse and pensioners would not be able to afford a decent standard of living if the country continued with taxpayer-funded pensions, ACT leader Richard Prebble said on Wednesday. Page 6.
Equities boost AMP Investments: AMP Investments has made bumper returns of 32.5 percent from New Zealand share investments in the June 1997 year. Page 27.
NPT unit placement approved: National Property Trust's unitholders on Wednesday approved issuing units to help buy a property in Wellington's "Golden Mile". Page 27.
Steel & Tube hopes to avoid job losses: Steel and Tube Holdings is looking at staff levels at Southern Cross Engineering's Christchurch and Hamilton factories. Page 27.
